Template literals are now masked like the other string literals, so two JavaScript functions that differ only inside a `` `...` `` literal normalize to the same body. I haven't tested that JavaScript case itself. I didn't add a test, and I didn't run a duplication report on such a pair.

The change is one line in `extraCleanContent` in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/units/CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java`. It replaces `` `...` `` with ` `` `. The pattern also matches across newlines, so multi-line literals are covered. It runs before the quote rules so an apostrophe inside a template, as in "don't", doesn't throw off the `'...'` masking. Differences in the code outside the literals still keep the units apart.

The existing `*Unit*` tests in `codeanalyzer` pass.
